notes.meaning: Moses and the people of Israel sang this song of praise right after crossing the Red Sea. They gave all the credit to the Lord for His glorious victory over the Egyptian army. God proved His power by throwing both the enemy horses and their riders into the deep water.

The people rejoiced that the Lord was their personal strength, their song, and their salvation. Salvation here means being rescued from danger and slavery. God was no longer just a story from their ancestors; He was their own living protector.

The Lord is praised as a mighty warrior who fights for His people and always wins. His name is Yahweh, the eternal and faithful God who keeps every promise He makes. Because He fought for Israel, they knew they did not win this battle by human strength.

Pharaoh sent his finest chariots and top army officers to crush the Israelites. God overturned all of them and drowned them in the Red Sea. In a single moment, the world's most powerful military force was completely broken.

The deep water closed in and covered the Egyptian soldiers completely. Weighed down by their heavy armor, they plunged to the bottom like stones. None of them could swim away or survive the rushing flood.

God showed His majestic power as if striking the enemy with a mighty right hand. In the Bible, the right hand stands for a warrior's main strength and skill. The Lord completely shattered the enemy without needing any human help.

In His great majesty, the Lord threw down everyone who dared to oppose Him. Standing against God's people was the same as standing against God Himself. His holy anger wiped them out as quickly as a brushfire burns up dry straw.

Poetic words describe how God used a strong wind like a blast of breath to push the sea aside. The waters piled high and stood firm on each side like solid walls. What was usually liquid became a pathway for His people to escape.

The Egyptian army boasted loudly about what they would do. They planned to chase down Israel, slaughter them, and take all their riches. Their pride made them blind to the danger of fighting against the Almighty.

With just a simple breath of wind from the Lord, the sea collapsed back into place. All the boasting of the Egyptian army came to an instant halt. They dropped like lead into the deep, churning waters.

No false god of the nations can be compared to the true Lord. He alone is completely holy, pure, and worthy of our deepest awe and worship. He performs great wonders that prove there is no other God beside Him.

The Lord stretched out His hand, and the watery depths swallowed up the entire Egyptian force. The seabed closed over them, putting an end to their cruelty forever. Their defeat showed that the earth and everything in it obeys God's command.

God showed loyal, unfailing love by leading the people He had purchased out of slavery. By His mighty strength, He began guiding them toward the sacred land where He would live among them. His past rescue gave them full confidence that He would finish what He started.

The surrounding pagan nations would soon hear reports of what God did at the sea. When the people of Philistia heard the news, they would shake with terror. They realized that no ordinary army could stand against a nation protected by the Lord.

The rulers of Edom and Moab would be overcome with dread when they saw Israel coming near. The inhabitants of Canaan would lose all heart and melt away in panic. What happened in Egypt sent a warning to all the idol-worshiping tribes along the way.

Great dread fell upon the enemy nations so they were frozen like stone. God kept them from attacking while His redeemed people marched safely toward their new home. His powerful arm made a secure path for Israel through dangerous territory.

The Lord promised to bring His people into the hill country of Canaan and plant them securely there. He planned a holy dwelling place where they could gather to worship Him in peace. His own hands would build and establish this sanctuary for them.

The song finishes with a loud shout that the Lord will reign as King forever and ever. Pharaoh was a powerful king on earth, but his rule came to a sudden end. God's kingdom and majesty will never pass away.

A brief summary explains why Israel sang this glorious song. When Pharaoh's chariots and cavalry chased into the sea bed, God rolled the deep waters back over them. Yet the Israelites had walked straight through the middle of the sea on dry ground.

Miriam took a tambourine in her hand and led the women in celebration. She is called a prophetess because God gave her special spiritual gifts and messages to share. The women followed her, playing their instruments and dancing with pure joy over God's victory.

Miriam led the women in singing back the main chorus to the men. They repeated the joyful truth that the Lord is highly exalted because He threw the enemy's horses and riders into the sea. Singing in responsive groups was a common way Israel celebrated big events.

Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea into the dry Desert of Shur. The people traveled under the burning sun for three full days without finding any water. After their great spiritual high at the sea, they faced a hard, practical trial in the wilderness.

When they finally found water, they were disappointed to discover it tasted bitter and mineral-heavy. Because of the bad taste, they named the place Marah, which means bitterness. Their joy turned into frustration as their thirst grew worse.

Instead of turning to God in prayer, the thirsty people turned on Moses and grumbled. They demanded to know what they were going to drink to survive. Hard times often show how quickly human hearts forget God's past blessings.

Moses cried out to the Lord for help, and God showed him a piece of wood to throw into the water. When Moses threw it in, God miraculously made the water fresh and sweet to drink. There the Lord also gave them a teaching to test their faith and obedience.

God promised that if the people listened closely and obeyed His laws, He would protect them from the terrible sicknesses He brought on Egypt. He revealed Himself by the special name, the Lord who heals you. Obedience to God brings real health and protection to His people.

Next, the people arrived at Elim, a lush desert oasis with twelve water springs and seventy palm trees. There was plenty of fresh water for every tribe and shade for their weary families. God brought them comfort and refreshment right after their time of testing.
